$comment: The source of sf-popover's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/popover (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

placement.summary: Where the surface stands beside the trigger: top, bottom, start or end, centred on it, or with -start or -end its start or end edge on the trigger's (inline-start and inline-end are start-start and end-start). Logical: start and end follow the writing direction. At the window's edge it moves along the trigger's edge, or to the other side.

label.summary: The accessible name of the surface. A surface with a role and no name is announced as an unnamed one.

width.summary: A width of its own. Left to its content a surface takes the width of its longest line, which a list of names makes wide and ragged.

offset.summary: The gap between the trigger and the surface: a token (var(--sf-space-1\/3)) or a CSS length. Left empty, the surface touches the trigger as before; with an arrow it is the arrow's reach.

arrow.summary: An arrow toward the trigger, off by default. It carries the surface's own shadow (the overlay shadow drawn as a filter over the surface and the arrow); with an arrow the surface does not scroll by itself, and the gap is the arrow's reach (space 1/2) unless offset gives one.

dismissible.summary: Esc and a press outside close it. A consumer that owns those keys turns this off and calls close() when it decides.

surface-role.summary: What the surface is to a reader: dialog, menu, listbox or group. Written on sf-popover; the surface gets the role and the trigger aria-haspopup.

open.summary: Whether the surface is shown. Reflected, so a consumer can read it and set it.

A request to open, sent before the surface opens (show(), toggle(), the trigger); cancelable -- preventDefault() keeps it closed and the call answers refused. sf-popover-opened follows once it is open.

opened.summary: The surface opened: sent after the open setting became true, by show() or by a page writing the setting.

close.summary: A request to close, sent before the surface closes (close(), toggle(), the trigger, Escape, a press outside); cancelable -- preventDefault() keeps it open. detail.reason says why. sf-popover-closed follows once it is closed.

closed.summary: The surface closed: sent after the open setting became false; detail.reason says why (api when a page wrote the setting).

toggle.summary: Open or close it; a boolean forces one or the other.

return-focus.summary: Put the focus back on the trigger.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16); it draws nothing: the trigger and the content are the page's own nodes, placed where they were written.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-popover for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (attribute rows), manifest-only (the DOM name does not change; its meaning does, so no shim).

rows.note: read by the popover, not the shim: role leaves the host once read (the shim would mirror that removal onto surface-role); each read is noted with these dates
the same DOM name is the cancelable request now (sent before opening); the fact is sf-popover-opened
the same DOM name is the cancelable request now (sent before closing, {reason, unsaved}); the fact is sf-popover-closed

x-summary: A surface anchored to a control the consumer supplies, with its own open state, dismissal and returned focus. Built as a general part because the Framework had the surface and not the behaviour: two composites wrote it by hand within a week, the second copying the first.
x-renamed: settings.role → surface-role: a host attribute, never a setting (§3.1); the attribute is a dated alias and leaves the host

events sf-popover-open, sf-popover-close: were facts sent after the state changed; by §19.3 and vocabulary §4 they are the cancelable requests now, and the facts are sf-popover-opened and sf-popover-closed
x-decisions: events: a layer asks before it closes (§19.3): sf-popover-close {reason, unsaved} is the cancelable request and sf-popover-closed {reason} the fact; sf-popover-open and sf-popover-opened likewise. The old names were facts with the same DOM names, so no alias can carry them: a listener of sf-popover-close now hears it just before the surface closes, without the element in detail (§8). No Framework code listened to them.
key-effects: the trigger is the page's own control; Enter and Space press it and toggle the surface (toggle:open); Escape closes while dismissible; Tab leaves it (the surface does not trap focus).
version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0: the attribute role is a dated alias of surface-role; added unsaved and the facts.
template: the template draws nothing; trigger and content stay the page's nodes where they were written (§4.5 place, never copy), and the stylesheet places them by data-open and data-placement.
examples: examples.json (a settings surface, a menu, a wide list); probe.json drives Enter, Escape and an outside press (gate 16).

css-variables: six public variables of the surface (background, colour, radius, shadow, max width, max height) read by default.css with the old internal --sf-popover--max-* and the elevation tokens as fallbacks (§6).

side-effects: none. The surface is drawn in place, absolutely positioned against the host, not at the end of body; it registers as a surface layer of the one stack (core open-surface-mark), so Escape and an outside press reach it only while it is the top layer.
dismissing: reasons escape (Escape), outside (a press outside), close (the trigger pressed again), api (a script); dismissible=false removes escape and outside.
docs: docs.md in the folder since 1.2.1 (simai/ui-source#30); ui-doc keeps the full page with its examples.

version 1.1.1: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.
version 1.1.5: the outcomes applied and refused come from core/js/element-manifest.js (core.runtime 1.25.0, duplication audit A-26) instead of a copy of its own; behaviour unchanged.

version 1.1.6: what the page sets inline on the host that a child inherits -- custom properties, colour, the font but its size -- stays on the host before its box (core.runtime 1.30.0, Smart base hostInheritedStyle), so el.style.color or a --var set on sf-popover reaches the trigger and the surface; before, the host's style attribute was replaced by the box alone.

version 1.2.0 (2026-11-07): a minor. The setting offset, the gap between the trigger and the surface as a token or a CSS length (simai/ui-source#69): the stylesheet reads it as --sf-popover--offset, a margin on the trigger side of whichever placement is set; empty, nothing changes. It declares static rendersNoTemplate, so its first DOM update counts as its render (Smart base, core.runtime 1.32.0): what it holds is read by the Loader then, and an sf-dropdown or sf-button-icon in it is defined (simai/ui-source#70).

version 1.2.1: the folder carries its docs.md (simai/ui-source#30): a kit audit that read the source docs took sf-popover as undocumented while ui-doc had its page. The docs say what the page says -- trigger and content in place, the settings, the open and close requests and facts with their reasons, the keys and the six public variables. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.2.2 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint snapshots follow the actions block (docs review R031, R032; decisions C13-C15): the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws ask for the screen-reader-only utility sheet (sf-button 1.9.0, sf-button-icon 1.7.0), an sf-button-close it draws asks for its own sheet (C14), and sf-input's classes follow its outer sizes (sf-input 1.6.0). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.3.2: the surface stands over the page: the overlay place (C20, the shadow system, owner 2026-11-08), --sf-shadow-overlay on --sf-surface-popup (a step lighter in the dark theme than the level-2 surface). --sf-popover-shadow still replaces it. Nothing else changes. Also: a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. The generated reference gives each action's method its one object argument, toggle({force}), close({reason}), where it read the parameters one by one (standard §4.4: the parameters arrive as one object); the element's code also takes the value alone, toggle(<boolean>), and the reference says so (x-registry.action-calls). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. The close action's reason is optional, as the element reads it (close() closes with reason api), so the reference no longer calls close's argument required. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.
version 1.4.1 (2026-11-09): the bubble declares a popup place and its ink is --sf-on-surface rather than inherited (C16, the background system, owner 2026-11-08).

version 1.4.2 (2026-11-10): a patch; nothing in the component changed. The menu it holds is sf-menu-context, which since 1.14.1 draws the context-menu frame without the late utility classes (relative, flex, flex-col, flex-1), so the first-paint snapshots follow; the component takes a patch with them. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.2 (2026-11-10): the bubble takes back --sf-surface-underlay (initial), as every place does (C43, owner 2026-11-10): a popover opened from a selected row does not lay its badges over the row's place. Nothing drawn differently. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.3 (2026-11-10): the bubble carries the dim ink on a fill one step up, dark tone 90 (C43, owner 2026-11-10), as every popup place does: a tonal quiet button's key read 4.25:1 on it. Light unchanged. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.4 (2026-11-10): the bubble re-declares the muted ink as its disabled ink (C43, owner 2026-11-10: --sf-on-surface-muted is var(--sf-on-surface-disabled), deprecated), so a reader of the former name inside a popover follows it. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.5 (2026-11-10, pair next integration): one number above every claim for the notes above, which separate branches each claimed: the menus snapshot patch (1.4.2) and the C43 bubble changes (1.4.2 underlay reset, 1.4.3 dim ink one step up in dark, 1.4.4 muted is the disabled ink). The integration had first numbered the two 1.4.2 notes 1.4.3, which C43 then claimed with other content. They ship together in this release; 1.4.2, 1.4.3 and 1.4.4 are never published alone. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.0 (2026-11-10): an open surface is kept on screen by the shared anchored positioning (core/js/position.js, Floating UI: flip and shift, as every other floating surface): it hangs from the corner its placement names and moves along the trigger's edge, or to the other side, when the window has no room there. Placed by the stylesheet alone, a 320px panel from a trigger near the window's edge ran past it (ui-doc «Рецепты», «Уведомления», 2026-11-10). With room it stands exactly where it stood; the offset stays the gap; it is not lifted into the top layer, so a window or a drawer opened from it is still drawn over it; closed, the inline placement is removed and the stylesheet's is back. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged; tests/browser/popover-on-screen.browser.mjs. (1.4.2 and 1.4.3 are taken on integration/pair-next.) A surface its consumer draws as a sheet (data-sf-sheet, sf-input-rich's link editor on a phone, C32 RT-02) is not anchored: the sheet rule places it, and the attribute is watched while the surface is open (pair next 2, DEV forms round 2 D3: the anchor held the phone sheet at the top of the screen).

version 1.5.0 (2026-11-10, C41 + C42, owner): the popup place in the template writes the neutral fill at 8/12/16 (was 16/20/24) and takes the theme's accent back (--sf-primary, -hover, -active, --sf-on-primary), as core sf-place does; a popup opened from the content is a nested popup: on the content's children --sf-surface-popup and its dim ink are the nested popup's (DEV surfaces audit defect 3).

version 1.5.0, also (2026-11-11, written on the pair's 1.5.0): the bubble declares --sf-surface-place-ground, the nearest opaque place, with its own colour, as every solid place does, so a status dot on a soft coloured place inside it lies over the bubble. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.1 (2026-11-12): a patch. A popup standing in a bg-surface-4 block is a nested popup again, and a nested popup draws its controls' edges in the nested-popup outline (Contrast R3b, R3-1 and R3-2); the template's sheet reads --sf-place--popup-outline. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.1, also (2026-11-11, contrast lows): the bubble writes out the theme's --sf-on-surface-hover and --sf-on-surface-active, which a strong place and glass now re-declare, and takes back --sf-place--container-outline, as every opaque place does. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.1, also (2026-11-11, contrast lows return): inside bg-surface-4 the content takes back the accent the step found (--sf-place--found-*), as every place there does, so a popover on the darkest light step keeps the page's primary and link tones. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.1, also (2026-11-11, C41 inverse places): the content takes the theme's accent and boundary line back on the inverse places too (bg-surface-inverse, bg-surface-inverse-fixed), as the mixin sf-place-back-on-colour writes it.

version 1.5.2 (2026-11-13, group build 2; written on the branch as 1.5.1, which the released pair already carries): a patch (owner decision C107, the icon colour; tokens.colour 1.13.0). The bubble is an opaque place and takes the theme's roles back: it now takes the fourth icon role too, --sf-on-surface-icon (neutral-25 light, neutral-80 dark), so a button's icon inside a popover opened on a coloured block is the half step under its label, not the coloured place's ink. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.2, also (2026-11-12, C43 later; written on the branch as 1.5.0): the bubble takes back --sf-surface-place-fill (initial) beside --sf-surface-underlay, as every place now does, so an anchored badge in a popover opened from a selected row does not ring with that row.

version 1.5.2, also (2026-11-13, C113, owner): the popup place in the template writes the neutral fill at 12/16/20 (was 8/12/16) and the disabled plate at 8 (was 12), as the core theme does; settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.6.0 (written on the branch as 1.5.0; 2026-11-11, C59 stage S1, owner decision): one positioning engine and the popover kind. An open surface stands in the browser's top layer (a manual popover, core/js/position.js liftToTopLayer): an ancestor's overflow: hidden, a scroll container, a z-index, a transform or contain no longer clip or cover it; it stays where it was written in the document, so the host's variables, theme, lang, dir and density reach it as before. It is placed by the Framework's floating-surface engine, core/js/float-anchor.js (internal: not on window.SF and not in the public JS API contract until the later kinds prove its shape; built on SF.Position's public API, position.js unchanged): CSS anchor positioning (anchor-name on the host, position-area, position-try-fallbacks flip-inline / flip-block) where the browser has it, Floating UI where it has not, and Floating UI for the rest of an opening when no CSS area keeps the surface inside the window (CSS has no shift); both flip and shift at the four edges and say the side they took in data-sf-side. While a window or a drawer stands above it in the layer stack (one opened from its content) it steps down out of the top layer, so the window is drawn over it, and back up when the window closes. Placement takes top, bottom, start and end (centred) and start-start, start-end, end-start, end-end beside the six it had (default bottom-end, unchanged). The setting arrow (boolean, off): a square of the surface's fill at the trigger's centre (--sf-position-arrow-x/-y from the engine), and the overlay shadow drawn as --sf-shadow-overlay-filter (drop-shadow, the same two layers as --sf-shadow-overlay) over the surface and the arrow; with an arrow the surface has no scroll of its own and the gap defaults to space 1/2. A dialog surface takes the focus a frame after show(), toggle() or the trigger opened it (unless its content took it); the trigger says aria-controls when the surface has an id. The dismissal stays the Framework's own (Escape and an outside press through the layer stack, cancelable sf-popover-close with its reasons): a native auto popover's light dismiss can be neither cancelled nor given a reason. sf-input-rich's phone sheet is held in the top layer by the popover while it is open. Events, values, keys and the six public variables unchanged; tests/browser/popover-top-layer.browser.mjs, tests/popover-top-layer.contract.test.mjs.

$comment: The popover loads on demand like any other Smart element. It renders no
markup and draws into no other component: what it owns is where the consumer's
own nodes are, said in attributes its stylesheet reads.

slots.description: The named slots the consumer fills.

trigger.description: The control that opens it, left where the consumer put it.

content.description: What the surface holds. This component claims nothing about its shape.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-popover for a surface anchored to a control the consumer supplies -- a field's settings, a filter, a list of things to add -- that opens on its trigger and closes on Escape or outside.
do_not: Do not use it for a blocking task; that is sf-modal
Do not write role on the host; use surface-role
Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component

accessibility.focus: label names the surface. surface-role sets the surface's role (dialog by default; menu, listbox, group); the trigger gets aria-haspopup to match, aria-expanded, and aria-controls when the surface has an id. Opening it with show(), toggle() or the trigger moves focus into a dialog surface (the surface itself, a frame later, unless its content took the focus first); a menu or a list moves its own. Tab goes on into its content and out to the page; Escape or a press outside closes it and returns focus to the trigger. While it is open a modal or drawer behind it leaves Escape alone.
